```console
# Protocol (fixed before any method was scored on targets)

Written 2026-11-26 before running `scripts/02_run.py`. Changes after seeing results are logged in the section "Deviations" at the end, with the reason.

## Data
13 binary matrices (7 Open LLM Leaderboard v2, 6 HELM) of `data.md`, commit 55faff49…; see `scripts/00_download.sh`, audit in `results/audit.csv`.
Pre-processing (`src/bpred/data.py`): OLL models repeated under the same name are dropped (keep first); any model whose response vector is identical to an earlier model's is dropped (keep first); items answered identically by all models are kept (they contribute zero variance and make the problem easier for no method in particular; counted in the audit). HELM row→model names come from `helm_model_list.txt` (83 rows); `legalbench` has 79 rows with no published row→name mapping, so its families are unknown (each row its own family; it is excluded from the lineage split and its extrapolation/interpolation CIs cluster by row).
Family = first matching keyword of the lower-cased model name (`family_of`, e.g. qwen, llama, mistral, openai-gpt, claude), else the organisation prefix. Heuristic; checked on the audit output.

## Splits (per benchmark; sources = models given to the method, targets = models only scored at the end)
- **interp** — random 5-fold over models (seed 0); targets = the fold, sources = the other 4 folds. Near-duplicates (same family) stay in the sources.
- **lineage** — 5-fold over *families* (families assigned to folds by greedy size balancing, seed 0); targets = the families of the fold, sources = every other family. Not run for legalbench.
- **extrap** — targets = the top 25 % of models by full-benchmark score, sources = the rest; hence every target is above every source (ties at the boundary resolved by dropping tied targets). One configuration per benchmark; subset draws are the only replication.
Thin cells: a (benchmark, split) with fewer than 10 targets or fewer than 5 independent families among targets is flagged "thin", excluded from the main aggregate and shown with them included as well.

## Budget and the primary endpoint
n grid {10, 25, 50, 100, 200, 400} restricted to n ≤ N/2 (so some small benchmarks have fewer points). **Primary n = 100** (reported with n/N). **Primary endpoint:** RMSE ratio to uniform random sampling at n = 100, where RMSE = sqrt(mean over targets and subset draws of (pred − true full score)²) per (benchmark, split) and ratio = RMSE_method / RMSE_uniform on the same draws and targets; aggregated by geometric mean over benchmarks (non-thin; plus all). CIs: bootstrap over families (resampling target families, with all draws of a family kept) — "paired" because the ratio is formed inside each bootstrap replicate. Everything else (MAE, signed bias, Spearman, Kendall, top-decile precision, pairwise order accuracy vs true gap δ, error vs true score) is secondary. Rank correlations: per (fold, draw) over targets, then averaged over folds and draws.
Draws: R = 10 independent subsets per (fold, n) for interp and lineage, R = 40 for extrap (single fold). One subset per draw serves all targets. Deterministic designs (info-top-n; CAT, which depends on the target only) have no draw variance; they count once.

## Methods (all selection/tuning uses sources only; target contributes its n answers; same n for every method; shared seeds)
Designs: `uniform`, `strat` (sorted-by-source-difficulty systematic: one random item per stratum of N/n items), `pps` (π_i = n[(1−ε)w_i/Σw + ε/N], w_i = √(p̂_i(1−p̂_i)), systematic PPS in difficulty order, π capped at 1), `balanced` (greedy forward selection from a random pool of 4n items so that the subset mean reproduces every source's full score), `anchor` (k-means with n clusters on the item×source response matrix, medoid per cluster, weight = cluster size), `infotop` (top-n items by 2PL Fisher information averaged over source abilities), `cat` (adaptive max-information 2PL, per target).
